title: Introduce stability layer for dedicated capacity and adaptive warmup
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a stability layer to Dedicated autoscaler: adaptive warmup for warm pools, scale-down grace window, soft-throttle fallback to preserve throughput SLAs, and sampled per-tenant utilization telemetry. Config knobs are behind feature flag `stability_layer_v1`.
description: Motivation: we observed repeated throughput regressions during scale-down and cold-start cycles on Dedicated clusters when tenants with bursty patterns decommit suddenly. This PR introduces a 'stability layer' between the autoscaler and the provisioner that reduces oscillation and preserves throughput SLAs during capacity transitions. Key ideas: 1) adaptive warmup: when new cards are provisioned into a warm pool we incrementally ramp concurrency targets over a tunable warmup period derived from observed tail-latency and model sequence-length distribution; 2) decommit grace window: avoid hard deallocations within a tenant-specific hysteresis window computed from recent utilization decay rates; 3) soft-throttle fallback: on sudden capacity contraction we prefer temporary token-level concurrency throttles (per-tenant) and micro-shed before evictions to avoid large latency spikes; 4) sampled telemetry: lightweight reservoir sampling of per-tenant utilization sketches to feed the autoscaler and downstream billing/alerting without full-card telemetry costs. Implementation: adds a new autoscaler/stability package (stability_layer.go) that wraps existing decision logic, a warmup controller (pkg/provision/warmup.go) to drive progressive concurrency targets, changes to the provisioner API to accept soft-throttle hints, and new metrics and traces (stability_* metrics and warmup events). All behavior is gated behind the feature flag `stability_layer_v1` with a rollout plan described below. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2389) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf bench and canary runs - [x] metrics + alerts - [x] docs for operator knobs - [x] feature-flagged rollout
commits: (1) initial stability layer scaffolding and interfaces; (2) adaptive warmup controller implementation and tests; (3) soft-throttle contract and provisioner adapter; (4) sampled util reservoir + metrics; (5) helm values and docs; (6) perf numbers and tuning; (7) refactor autoscaler entrypoints to plug stability layer
review_conversation: Diego: Can you clarify how the decommit grace window is calculated? Maya: The window is computed from an exponential smoother of per-tenant utilization slope; we default to max(30s, 3x smoothed decay half-life) and it is configurable. Lina: Is soft-throttle observable to users? Maya: Yes, we emit stability.soft_throttle.active and per-tenant throttled_tokens_count; operator docs added. Owen: Concern about billing/chargebacks—will sampled telemetry be sufficient? Maya: We deliberately keep full billing telemetry unchanged; sampled sketches are for autoscaler heuristics and can be turned off. Diego: Please add a safety limit to avoid indefinite warm pools. Maya: Added a configurable max_warm_age and an automated reclamation path in warmup.go. Lina: Tests look good, but add a canary rollout plan. Maya: Added rollout_plan in PR which includes staged canary and automated rollback on alert triggers. Owen: Approving after CI green.
performance_summary: Local perf lab: reduced 95th token latency spikes during scale-down by ~38% and end-to-end tail P95 for multi-tenant bench by 22%. Cost delta on steady-state traffic: +0.7% for warm pool retention at default settings; prevented two incidents in internal canary (estimated avoidance of ~1800 failed requests).
rollout_plan: 1) Enable `stability_layer_v1` in staging for 24h on a single fleet; 2) run synthetic burst generator for 48h and monitor stability.* metrics + p95 token latency; 3) Canary enable on 5% of Dedicated fleets with linked alerting (autoscaler-sla-deviation); 4) Gradually increase to 30% over 72h if no regressions; 5) Full rollout to Dedicated after 7d and retrospective tuning; rollback: toggle feature flag off and scale warm pools down via reclamation job.
tests: Unit coverage: autoscaler/stability 87% branch coverage; integration: warmup path + soft-throttle adapter simulated across scaled-up clusters; e2e: canary harness verifies no >2x SLA breaches during forced decommit events. CI: all checks passed including lint, go-test, integration-suite, and canary-smoke.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: core autoscaler heuristics are unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. The stability layer exposes a small set of knobs designed for operators: max_warm_age, warmup_target_fraction, decommit_hysteresis_base, soft_throttle_floor. Immutable model-serving contracts were preserved; provisioner changes are additive and backward-compatible.
operational_impact: Operators will get extra metrics and a new helm value group under `stabilityLayer.*`. Default values keep behavior off. Expected operator actions: tune warmup_target_fraction for high-burst tenants and set max_warm_age to control memory footprint.
follow_up: ENG-2420 follow-up will add automatic knob tuning using a small MLE to set warmup length per-model family and add finer-grained per-card eviction scoring.
acknowledgements: Thanks to SRE (Lina) for alert tuning guidance, Provisioning (Owen) for adapter work, and Bench team for synthetic harness runs.
